launch.name: Work Orca
launch.summary: Orca on the default profile (%APPDATA%\orca), full screen 1, holding the work repos that `devenv orca apply` registers. Replaces the Workspace Terminal columns. Listed before Personal Orca so a fresh logon launches it first: each launch waits for a window that was not open before it, so the two Orca windows cannot swap. On a re-run `window_pid_file` picks the window owned by the pid this profile records in orca-runtime.json.

launch.name: Personal Orca
launch.summary: Orca on a second profile (`--user-data-dir`), full screen 3, holding the personal repos that `rig estate orca --apply` registers. Orca is one window per profile, so a second window needs a second profile. Orca's in-app update relaunches only the profile that ran it, so rig applies updates instead: restore installs a staged update while no Orca is running, and `desktop-manager workspace update-orca` closes both profiles, installs and relaunches both. If an in-app update closes this one anyway, the next restore finds no orca-runtime.json pid for it and launches it.

launch.name: Workspace Terminal 1
launch.summary: First of the side-by-side Windows Terminal sessions on screen 1, in columns at least 800px wide: three on the 2560px main screen, two on a 1920px one. Replaces the paired Warp sessions after Warp kept killing long-running Claude sessions mid-run. Unlike Warp on Windows, `wt-pwsh` can auto-run the terminal command, so `claude` starts in the workspace root without a manual step. At logon the command is deferred: the shell opens bare and `claude-sessions startup` resumes a session that died into it, or starts `claude` fresh. `--title` gives each window a distinct anchor; wt-pwsh terminals are force-relaunched rather than reused, so title drift once Claude renames the window does not accumulate duplicates.

launch.name: Workspace Terminal 2
launch.summary: Second side-by-side Windows Terminal session on screen 1, column 2.

launch.name: Workspace Terminal 5
launch.summary: Third column on screen 1, opened only when the screen is wide enough for three 800px columns (the 2560px main screen); a narrower screen 1 leaves it out for that run.

launch.name: Work Browser - Work Profile
launch.summary: Full-screen Chrome (work profile) on screen 2, between the terminal pairs, replacing Fork now that the Review desktop owns Fork. `--new-window` forces a fresh window instead of focusing an existing work-profile one on the Admin desktop; reuse only considers chrome.exe windows already on this desktop, so the Admin desktop's Chrome windows are never claimed. Roll back with `--enable work-fork --disable work-chrome`.

launch.name: Fork
launch.summary: PAUSED (feature `work-fork` is off) - Fork now lives on the Review desktop and Chrome takes this slot. Kept so the old layout can be restored with `--enable work-fork --disable work-chrome`.

launch.name: Workspace Terminal 3
launch.summary: First of two side-by-side Windows Terminal sessions on screen 3, replacing the single full-screen Warp window that hosted Claude sessions as tabs. Two half-width windows per screen means a crash takes one session rather than every tab in one window.

launch.name: Workspace Terminal 4
launch.summary: Second side-by-side Windows Terminal session on screen 3, slot 2.

launch.name: Warp Workspace 1
launch.summary: PAUSED (feature `warp-terminals` is off) — kept so the Warp layout can be restored with `--enable warp-terminals --disable wt-terminals`. First of two side-by-side Warp sessions on screen 1. Each plain warp.exe launch opens a NEW window (verified 2026-07-03), and Warp honors the launch working directory on Windows even though it ignores warp:// launch configs — so `cwd` opens this window in the workspace root (its title becomes 'pwsh in workspace'). Warp still can't auto-run a command on Windows, so run `claude` yourself. Slot 1/slot 2 placement disambiguates the two warp.exe windows on restore.

launch.name: Warp Workspace 2
launch.summary: PAUSED (feature `warp-terminals` is off). Second side-by-side Warp session on screen 1. Plain warp.exe relaunch opens a distinct new window (Warp on Windows is not single-window on launch), placed in slot 2. `cwd` opens it in the workspace root; run `claude` yourself.

launch.name: Warp (Claude experiment)
launch.summary: PAUSED (feature `warp-terminals` is off). Full-screen Warp on screen 3, to experiment with managing several Claude sessions as Warp tabs. Launched plain (no new-window URI) so exactly one window opens and placement can resize it; passing a warp:// URI makes Warp spawn extra unplaced windows. `cwd` opens this window in the workspace root — without it Warp inherits the launcher's cwd (e.g. System32 when the logon scheduled task starts it). Warp on Windows still can't auto-run a command on launch, so run `claude` yourself. Shares window_title 'workspace' with the two side-by-side Warp entries: all three windows are titled 'pwsh in workspace', so without a title this entry was disqualified from reuse (its window title contains a sibling's 'workspace' title) and relaunched a duplicate every restore attempt; the shared title anchor plus its distinct screen-3 placement lets reuse claim the right window.
